title: Normalized internal quotient/principal cone comparison
statement: Fix l,E,X,A,d and its pointwise uniformizer property as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] and [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution]. For every K-flat unbounded cochain complex P in A, there is an isomorphism c:Q(completion(scalarOnComplex(d,P))) ~= Q(roos(P)), for the principal cone construction [def-pur-principal-cone-tower] and the fixed internal quotient Roos construction [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], with Q(unit(scalarOnComplex(d,P))) >> c.hom = Q(augmentation(P)). This equality specifies the actual zero-homotopy augmentation, not merely its composites with quotient projections.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, regular singleton Koszul-to-quotient comparison; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941, normalized product-cone computation; coefficient regularity and the internal tower are as in sk-def-pe-derived-completion and det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution.

proof.text: For each n use the normalized one-level internal augmentation. Its component is the unshifted cone projection followed by the specified levelUnit. On each cone summand, the (mu,1) transition commutes with this map: the shifted component is zero, and the unshifted component follows from levelUnit_step. The inclusion also composes to levelUnit exactly.

Take the product of these maps. Tower-transition naturality makes it commute with the two 1-shift maps. CountableAB4Star for the internal module category follows from Mod.epi_π_app_zero and pro-etale repleteness, as in DerivedCompletion. Mathlib quasiIso_limMap makes the product a quasi-isomorphism. The morphism of cone triangles then gives a quasi-isomorphism of cones; shift by minus one and localize. Product extensionality gives the equation of product units. Naturality of the zero-cochain cocone lift gives equality of the entire units.

Use the existing genericCoconeIso of DerivedCompletion to identify the quotient mapping cocone with the fixed explicit Roos coordinates. Its first coordinate is mappingCocone.fst and its second is minus mappingCocone.snd. The zero-cochain lift therefore maps exactly to (unitProduct,0), by both biproduct projections. Localize and compose with the product-cone isomorphism to obtain the claimed augmented derived isomorphism.

theorem internal_quotient_principal_cone_comparison
    (d : End (Mod.regular (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E)))
    (hd : ∀ (S : Profinite.{u}ᵒᵖ) (f : (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E).obj.obj S)
      (s : S.unop), ((d.hom.hom.app S) f).down s =
        Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E * f.down s)
    (P : CochainComplex (Modules l E X) ℤ)
    (hP : (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (Modules l E X) (.up ℤ)).kFlat P) :
    ∃ c : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (CochainComplex.PrincipalCone.completion
        (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X d P)) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (roos l E X P),
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainComplex.PrincipalCone.unit
        (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X d P)) ≫ c.hom =
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (augmentation l E X P)
